count_reason: Fifteen separate failure ideas matter for a blind walking robot on this plant route: grip, trips, snags, body strikes, climbs, tight passages, blockage, load and turning. Three or four severity levels each gives 49 worlds. Gravity was left out because it does not vary in a plant.

scenarios.name: floor_damp_film
scenarios.reason: A slightly slick floor reduces the grip margin the policy relies on when it pushes off and turns.

scenarios.name: floor_oily_film
scenarios.reason: A thin oil film across the floor could make the feet slide during the two corners.

scenarios.name: floor_greasy
scenarios.reason: A greasy floor may give too little grip for stance feet to hold while the body moves forward.

scenarios.name: floor_very_slick
scenarios.reason: A nearly frictionless floor could let the feet slip out from under the body and cause a fall.

scenarios.name: leak_across_straight
scenarios.reason: A sudden change to a slick puddle on the straight can surprise a policy that cannot see it.

scenarios.name: leak_at_first_corner
scenarios.reason: Turning on a slick puddle needs sideways grip that the feet may not have at the first corner.

scenarios.name: leak_under_left_legs
scenarios.reason: Slick ground under only the left legs creates uneven grip that may yaw the body or tip it.

scenarios.name: leak_before_cable_ramp
scenarios.reason: A slick puddle right before the cable ramp may cost the feet their grip just as the climb begins.

scenarios.name: small_drain_pipe_on_floor
scenarios.reason: A small pipe on the floor can catch a swinging foot that has no warning of it.

scenarios.name: water_pipe_on_floor
scenarios.reason: A pipe about as high as the normal foot lift may stop the swing leg and trip the robot.

scenarios.name: process_pipe_on_floor_second_leg
scenarios.reason: A taller pipe placed soon after the first turn must be crossed while the gait is still settling.

scenarios.name: large_header_pipe_on_floor
scenarios.reason: A large pipe 40 cm tall could be higher than a blind step can clear and may block the robot.

scenarios.name: pipe_just_above_robot
scenarios.reason: A pipe just above the robot may clear the body or strike its top during normal body bounce.

scenarios.name: pipe_at_top_of_body
scenarios.reason: A pipe at the height of the upper body can hit the robot, which has no way to know to crouch.

scenarios.name: pipe_at_body_centre
scenarios.reason: A pipe at body height may stop the robot outright or push it backward until it falls.

scenarios.name: pipe_at_shin_height
scenarios.reason: A raised pipe at shin height can hook a swinging leg instead of being stepped over.

scenarios.name: pipe_at_knee_height
scenarios.reason: A pipe at knee height could trap a leg between the pipe and the body as the robot moves on.

scenarios.name: pipe_under_belly
scenarios.reason: A pipe just under the belly may pass the body yet catch the thighs or scrape the underside.

scenarios.name: narrow_low_dropped_tray
scenarios.reason: A low tray with loose cables gives an uneven foothold that can turn a foot on landing.

scenarios.name: medium_dropped_tray
scenarios.reason: A tray 10 cm high and half a metre wide may trip a foot or leave it landing on the rungs.

scenarios.name: wide_tall_tray_at_angle
scenarios.reason: A wide, tall tray lying at an angle meets each leg at a different time and may upset the gait.

scenarios.name: crossover_shallow_steps
scenarios.reason: Even shallow steps may catch the toes of a blind policy that expects mostly level ground.

scenarios.name: crossover_typical_steps
scenarios.reason: Typical plant stair rises could stop the feet or cause a stumble on the way up or down.

scenarios.name: crossover_steep_steps
scenarios.reason: Tall, steep steps may exceed what the swing foot reaches and could pitch the robot on the descent.

scenarios.name: crossover_very_tall_steps
scenarios.reason: Steps of 25 cm are likely too tall for a blind climb and may cause a block or a tumble.

scenarios.name: crossover_barely_wider_than_robot
scenarios.reason: Handrails barely wider than the robot can catch the hips or feet, since it cannot centre itself by sight.

scenarios.name: crossover_tight_passage
scenarios.reason: A tight passage leaves little room for sideways drift before a leg hits a handrail post.

scenarios.name: crossover_modest_passage
scenarios.reason: A modest width may still let foot placement drift into the rails during the step transitions.

scenarios.name: cable_ramp_about_11_degrees
scenarios.reason: A moderate slope shifts weight toward the rear legs and tests the balance of a level-ground gait.

scenarios.name: cable_ramp_about_20_degrees
scenarios.reason: A slope near 20 degrees with sharp crests may scrape the belly or pitch the body at each edge.

scenarios.name: cable_ramp_about_31_degrees
scenarios.reason: A slope near 31 degrees may make the robot slide back on the way up or tip forward on the way down.

scenarios.name: worn_rubber_ramp
scenarios.reason: A worn ramp surface on a gentle slope may lower grip enough for the feet to creep downhill.

scenarios.name: wet_steel_ramp
scenarios.reason: A wet steel slope near 14 degrees leaves little spare grip and may send the robot sliding back.

scenarios.name: oily_plate_ramp
scenarios.reason: An oily plate on even a mild slope may offer less grip than the slope demands, so the feet slide.

scenarios.name: fine_low_bars
scenarios.reason: Closely spaced low bars change foot contact in many small jolts that could unsettle the gait.

scenarios.name: foot_sized_bar_gaps
scenarios.reason: Bars spaced near the foot size can wedge a foot in a gap or tilt it as it lands.

scenarios.name: tall_wide_bars
scenarios.reason: Tall, widely spaced bars can act like repeated small steps and may trip a foot with no warning.

scenarios.name: cabinet_near_miss
scenarios.reason: A cabinet close beside the route may be clipped by a swinging leg when the robot drifts slightly.

scenarios.name: cabinet_clips_shoulder
scenarios.reason: A cabinet overlapping the robot's width will strike one shoulder and may spin it off the route.

scenarios.name: cabinet_blocks_route
scenarios.reason: A cabinet squarely on the route cannot be seen or avoided, so the robot may push against it and fall or time out.

scenarios.name: small_valve_on_route
scenarios.reason: A small valve and handwheel on the route can catch a foot or shin as the robot walks over it.

scenarios.name: medium_valve_off_centre
scenarios.reason: A medium valve slightly off centre may snag the legs on one side and turn the robot off its line.

scenarios.name: large_valve_after_turn
scenarios.reason: A large valve just before the second corner may hit the belly and legs and stop the robot from passing.

scenarios.name: light_sensor_box
scenarios.reason: A light sensor box the policy never trained with slightly shifts balance and adds load through the route.

scenarios.name: heavy_sensor_box
scenarios.reason: A heavier box raises leg load and moves the balance point, which may upset the ramp climb.

scenarios.name: overweight_sensor_box
scenarios.reason: A box this heavy may exceed what the leg motors can carry and cause the body to sag or collapse.

scenarios.name: zigzag_on_damp_floor
scenarios.reason: Repeated sharp direction changes on a damp floor demand sideways grip that may run out.

scenarios.name: hairpin_on_oily_floor
scenarios.reason: A near reversal on an oily floor may make the robot skid or overshoot while it turns around.

scenarios.name: tight_zigzag_on_greasy_floor
scenarios.reason: Tight zigzags on a greasy floor leave no time to recover from one slip before the next turn begins.

not_tested.reason: Every object added here is static, so workers, forklifts and other moving hazards cannot be placed on the route.
The route follower is given its pose, and no function adds drift, dropouts or noisy joint and body readings.
No function can weaken a motor, overheat a joint or lower the battery during a walk.

not_tested.factor: Sideways shoves and gas or steam jets
not_tested.reason: No function applies an outside force to the body, so bumps from people or jets from a leak are missing.
Objects and floor are rigid, so sagging plates, soft mats, loose cables and mud cannot be represented.
Objects behave as fixed, so a tray or panel that shifts, tips or falls under a foot is not covered.
A leak is only a thin slippery layer, so standing water, thick sludge and water getting into hardware are missing.
The functions cannot make pits, missing grating panels or open floor drops for a foot or the robot to fall into.
Dust, heat, darkness and corrosive air affect hardware and any cameras, but they are not part of this physics world.
The list covers walking only, so sensor reading quality and inspection tasks at stops are not measured.
The function exists, but it was left out because gravity does not change at a plant site.
